title: CFM56-7B nacelle (Boeing 737NG) — technical data
description: Reference data on the propulsion installation used as the model's prototype: the nacelle of the CFM56-7B engine on the Boeing 737-600/-700/-800/-900. Every numeric value carries a citation and a confidence marker: documented — stated directly in the source, derived — obtained by measuring a scaled Boeing drawing (the method is described in measurement_method).
units: SI (metres, kilograms, degrees); the original figures from the source are given in brackets

identification.manufacturer: CFM International (GE Aerospace + Safran Aircraft Engines)
identification.nacelle_design_authority: Boeing (author of the technical requirements and of the nacelle shape)

nacelle_manufacturer.value: UTC Aerospace Systems (UTAS) — formerly Rohr Inc. / Goodrich Aerostructures, now Collins Aerospace (RTX)
nacelle_manufacturer.note: NTSB: «Boeing created the design specifications for the inlet. UTC Aerospace Systems (UTAS) was the inlet manufacturer» — the same applies to the fan cowls

nacelle_development_period.note: The structure and materials are close to the 737-300 nacelle (CFM56-3)

nacelle_overall_dimensions.comment: Nacelle dimensions. The key published value is the callout «APPROX 8 FT (2.44 M)» on the front view in the Boeing ACAP; it is placed exactly between the outer contours of the nacelle (verified by pixel-wise alignment of the extension lines with the outline: discrepancy < 0.05 m).

max_width.tolerance: ±0.15 m (±6 in — the stated accuracy of the ACAP drawings)
max_width.note: Maximum transverse dimension of the nacelle (largest horizontal diameter), front view, §2.2.5

max_width_measured.note: Outline measured on the front view: left nacelle 22.8 pt, right 22.6 pt at a scale of 0.1107 m/pt. Consistent with the 2.44 m callout within the tolerance of the drawing

max_height.note: Vertical dimension on the front view; the top of the nacelle is partly obscured by the outline of the wing and the pylon, so this is a lower-bound estimate

flat_bottom_width.note: Width of the flattened («hamster pouch») part of the lower generatrix on the front view

length_lip_to_fan_nozzle_exit.note: From the intake leading edge to the fan nozzle exit (end of the reverser) — side view, break in the lower contour at x=289.4 pt

length_lip_to_core_nozzle_exit.note: From the intake leading edge to the core nozzle exit — second break in the contour at x=297.3 pt

length_lip_to_plug_tip.note: Overall length of the propulsion installation including the plug

inlet_opening_diameter_as_drawn.note: Inner circle of the intake on the front view. For comparison: the fan diameter is 1.549 m; the ACAP drawing is schematic in small details

fineness_ratio.note: Ratio of length (to the core nozzle exit, 4.05 m) to maximum width (2.44 m)

not_published: Exact diameter at the intake highlight
Lengths of individual nacelle assemblies (intake / cowls / reverser) in the specifications
Masses of nacelle components — not published in open Boeing/CFM sources

ground_clearance.comment: Distance from the ground to the lowest point of the nacelle (the «D ENGINE» row in the Ground Clearances tables). ±3 inches for variation in loading, strut and tyre pressures.
ground_clearance.tolerance_note: CLEARANCES SHOWN ARE NOMINAL. ADD PLUS OR MINUS 3 INCHES (±0.076 m)

engine_tilt.note: The engines are carried forward and raised to the level of the upper wing surface; the tilt improves ground clearance, deflects the jet downwards and reduces heating of the pylon

engine_centreline_spacing.note: Between the axes of the left and right engines, measured on the front view

main_gear_track_reference.note: Used as a scale reference when measuring the drawing

flat_bottom_rationale.value: The 737 wing sits low above the ground. To fit a high-bypass engine, the bottom of the nacelle and the intake lip were flattened and the accessory gearbox and accessories were moved to the sides of the engine — hence the characteristic «hamster pouch» silhouette

nacelle_asymmetry.value: The 737NG nacelles have an asymmetric fan cowl and a flat bottom to suit the CFM56-7B
nacelle_asymmetry.quote: Boeing 737NG-series airplanes have an asymmetric fan cowl and a flat-bottom nacelle to accommodate the requirements of the CFM56-7B engine

structure.value: Inlet lip, inner and outer barrels, forward and aft bulkheads, attach ring

d_duct_assembly.value: The inlet lip together with the forward bulkhead forms a D-shaped contour (D-duct) — the cavity of the anti-icing system

inner_barrel.value: Acoustic honeycomb core, perforated skin and back skin; two bolted splice straps at 3 and 9 o'clock

containment_shield.original: about the aft 11 inches of the inner barrel
containment_shield.note: Aluminium anti-shrapnel shield bonded over the aft ~11 inches of the inner barrel

outer_barrel.value: Three panels with two structural frames

attachment.value: The attach ring at the rear of the intake bolts to flange A1 of the engine fan case; this joint is critical for fan blade-out (FBO) resistance

reference_distance_a1_flange.original: about 17 inches forward of the fan case A1 flange
reference_distance_a1_flange.note: The location where the inner barrel failed in the SWA1380 event — an indirect dimensional reference for the depth of the intake

function.value: Aerodynamic fairing over the fan case and the engine accessories; runs from the trailing edge of the intake to the leading edge of the reverser

halves.note: Inboard and outboard doors, the structure is asymmetric

hinges_per_half.note: Hinged at the top on the fan cowl support beam of the pylon

latches.note: Latches at the bottom at roughly 6 o'clock (hook plus keeper)

forward_locators.note: Axial locators on the leading edge, mating with the aft bulkhead of the intake

radial_restraint.value: A radial restraint at the bottom of the cowl engages a bracket on the fan case — it holds the shape of the cowl (a consequence of the flat nacelle bottom and the asymmetry of the cowl)

type.value: Cascade-type thrust reverser of the bypass duct with a translating sleeve and blocker doors

mounting.value: The reverser halves, like the fan cowls, are hinged on the pylon

role_in_nacelle.value: The reverser is structurally part of the nacelle and forms its aft section (the bypass duct)

design_note.value: The lengthened 737NG nacelle improved cruise performance: better internal flow organisation and reduced cruise drag

not_published: Axial length of the cascade band
Angle the cascades turn the flow through

plug.value: A conical plug that protrudes about 0.9–1.0 m beyond the core nozzle exit

exhaust_note.value: The streams are not mixed: the bypass duct exhausts coaxially, there is no mixer (unlike the JT8D)

pylon.value: The pylon (strut) carries the engine under the wing; it also carries the fan cowl support beam and the reverser hinge fittings. The pylon houses the aircraft model sensor by which the EEC limits the maximum certificated thrust

engine_reference_data.comment: Data on the engine itself — context for the nacelle dimensions

spinner.value: A conelliptical spinner — a compromise between ice shedding and a small flow stagnation zone (unlike the conical spinner of the early 737-300/400)

required_changes: New crushable spacers attaching the intake to the fan case, with increased fastener load capacity
Rework of the fan cowl radial restraint fitting and of the cowl ventilation
Strengthened bolts of the fan cowl support beam
Structural reinforcement in the area where the exhaust nozzle attaches
faa_ad_2025_nacelle.cause: Uncontained CFM56-7B fan blade failure, Southwest Airlines flight 1380, 17 April 2018

measurement_method.why: Boeing and CFM do not publish nacelle dimensions in their specifications. The only published value is a callout on the ACAP drawing; the remaining dimensions were obtained by measuring that same scaled drawing.
measurement_method.source_drawing: Boeing D6-58325-7 Rev C (October 2025), §2.2.5 «General Dimensions: Model 737-800» — top, side and front views
procedure: The drawing page was rasterised at 576 dpi (8× the 72 dpi base)
The aircraft outline was isolated by colour (the blue drawing lines separated from the black callouts and dimension lines)
The scale was established from three independent references on the drawing itself: main gear track 5.72 m, wheelbase 15.60 m, wing span 34.32 m
The resulting scales agreed within 1.3 %; the mean was adopted: 0.013836 m/pixel (0.1107 m per PDF point)
The nacelle dimensions were taken as extremes of the outline: width and height on the front view, lengths and contour breaks (nozzle exits) on the side view
measurement_method.validation: The extension lines of the «APPROX 8 FT (2.44 M)» dimension coincided with the outer contours of the nacelle to better than 0.05 m — which confirms that this callout refers to the width of the nacelle. The measured width of 2.50 m agrees with it within the tolerance of the drawing.
